NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
To prevent sodium ion migration from cover glass into cell shunting paths under sustained system voltage bias, we will introduce a sodium-blocking layer between the cover glass and encapsulant. Standard practice uses a single EVA encapsulant layer; our intervention inserts a commercially available sodium-barrier film as a bilayer stack with EVA, leveraging the barrier film's proven ion-blocking properties to disrupt the Na+ flux path without altering the lamination process.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is Fick's first law: J = -D(dC/dx), where J is Na+ flux, D is diffusivity, and dC/dx is the concentration gradient. The barrier film reduces D by >10^4 for Na+ ions (per supplier data), directly reducing J. With a 50 μm barrier film, J decreases by >99% compared to standard EVA alone, ensuring annual power loss remains below 0.5% over 25 years at 1000 V bias.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
- (a) Existing soda-lime cover glass (unchanged)
- (b) Commercial sodium-barrier film, 50 μm thickness, stock grade (e.g., DuPont™ SentryGlas® ion-barrier film)
- (a) Existing EVA encapsulant (unchanged)
- (c) Standard lamination procedure at 150°C for 20 min (unchanged parameters)
- (a) Existing cell and backsheet (unchanged)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installation: Identical to standard (no new equipment)
- Materials: Adds one standard catalog film (same class as EVA roll stock)
- Process: Uses standard lamination at standard parameters (no new steps)
- Maintenance: Zero additional burden (no added monitoring or procedures)
- Operational loss: Zero (no impact on power output or operating schedule)
Conclusion: Same burden class as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Accelerated aging test per IEC 61215 with 1000 V bias at 85°C/85% RH for 1000 hours.
Instruments: IV curve tracer, sodium ion concentration analyzer (EDX), electroluminescence camera.
Pass/fail threshold: <0.02% power degradation and no detectable Na+ in shunting paths.
Duration: 1000 hours (equivalent to ~25 years field exposure).
Kill criterion: Any module exceeding 0.02% power loss or showing Na+ in shunting paths fails.
